criteria.text: Adult maintenance treatment of moderately to severely active UC or CD following IV infliximab (FDA indications; approval #3).
Patient is 18 years or older (FDA labeled age; approval #1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a gastroenterologist (approval #2).
Received IV infliximab for ≥10 weeks and demonstrated a positive clinical response (approval #4).
Patient is not and will not be on concurrent treatment with another biologic agent (e.g. TNF-inhibitory, interleukin inhibitor, biologic response modifier; approval #5).
Evaluated and screened for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B virus infection prior to initiating treatment (approval #6).
No history of moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (denial #4).
No history of congestive heart failure (CHF) (denial #5).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Zymfentra Criteria Version 1: Original 03/12/2025; Accepted 04/18/2025; Effective 06/01/2025.

Zymfentra is a TNF blocker for SC maintenance after IV infliximab. Both adult UC and CD indications share all encoded criteria. Diagnosis severity is covered by the closed indication labels. Denial #1 is failure to meet approval criteria.
Duration (notes only): authorization up to 12 months. The PDF does not specify a separate initial/reauthorization split.
Quantity and dosing (manual review): 2 prefilled pens or syringes every 28 days; maximum dose 120 mg every 14 days (120 mg q14d ceiling). Quantity metadata does not numerically enforce these limits.

Cautions (notes only): increased malignancy risk, including lymphoma; monitor hepatic enzymes and liver function tests every 3 to 4 months due to severe hepatic reaction risk; increased severe infection risk; avoid live vaccines during treatment.

PDL context: Zymfentra is non_preferred. Preferred cytokine peers without rule packs (e.g. Humira, Hadlima, Rinvoq) are notes only. Linked alternatives require their own criteria review. IV Infliximab is a separate partial peer with its own criteria.
This pack remains partial: duration, dosing, quantity enforcement, monitoring and cautions require manual review.
